title: Air India Begins Boeing 787 Modifications After FAA Flags Door Handle Detachment Risk
excerpt: The airline is carrying out phased modifications to some of its 35 Dreamliners after the US aviation regulator issued an airworthiness directive over door assist handles that could pull loose during pre-flight checks.
body:
• Air India is modifying some of its 35 Boeing 787 Dreamliners after the US Federal Aviation Administration issued an airworthiness directive over door assist handles that could detach during pre-flight checks.
  • The FAA directive covers certain Boeing 787-8, 787-9, and 787-10 models worldwide — not just Air India's fleet.
  • Air India says there is no impact on current flight operations or safety; modifications are being done in a phased manner.
  • Air India's Dreamliner fleet includes 26 legacy Boeing 787-8s and 9 Boeing 787-9s, six of which came from the former Vistara.

Air India is carrying out modifications to some of its Boeing 787 Dreamliners after the US Federal Aviation Administration issued an airworthiness directive flagging a potential problem with door assist handles on certain 787 models, according to sources cited by PTI.

The FAA adopted the directive earlier this month for certain Boeing 787-8, 787-9, and 787-10 aircraft after reports that door assist handles had pulled loose from their lower attach points during pre-flight inspections. The regulator warned that a detached handle could injure passengers, crew, or maintenance personnel when opening the door and could limit exit during a time-limited emergency evacuation.

Phased Modifications Under Way

Air India currently operates 35 Dreamliners: 26 legacy Boeing 787-8s and 9 Boeing 787-9s. Of the 787-9 variants, three are newly delivered aircraft, while the remaining six were inherited from the now-merged Vistara. The airline's total fleet stands at 185 aircraft, including both narrow-body and wide-body planes.

"The regulator warned that a detached handle could injure passengers, crew, or maintenance personnel when opening the door and could limit exit during a time-limited emergency evacuation."

Sources told PTI that Air India is aware of the directive and that there is no impact on current flight operations or safety. The airline is carrying out the necessary modifications in a phased manner, and work has already been completed on some of the legacy aircraft. The exact number of planes requiring modifications has not been disclosed.

Neither Air India nor Boeing has issued official comments on the matter.

A Global Issue, Not an Air India Problem

The FAA directive applies to all operators of the affected Boeing 787 variants worldwide, not specifically to Air India. The issue surfaced during routine pre-flight checks across multiple airlines and relates to the door assist handle's lower attachment mechanism, not the door structure itself.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=m30TqvuF2TU

This is distinct from the broader Boeing door and fuselage safety concerns that have dominated aviation headlines since the Alaska Airlines 737 MAX 9 door-plug blowout in January 2024. The 787 handle issue is less severe in nature — it does not involve structural integrity of the aircraft or in-flight failure — but the FAA has nonetheless mandated corrective action to prevent injury risk.

What It Means for Travellers

Air India's Dreamliner fleet is central to its long-haul operations, serving key routes between India and the United States, Europe, and the Asia-Pacific region. These are among the most heavily used routes by NRI and diaspora travellers. The airline has said the modifications will not disrupt its flight schedule.

The phased approach means Air India is pulling aircraft from service briefly for the fix and returning them, rather than grounding a portion of its fleet. For passengers, the practical impact should be minimal — no route cancellations or schedule changes have been announced.

Air India, now under the Tata Group, is in the middle of a broader fleet renewal and cabin retrofit programme. The airline recently began operating its first fully customised Boeing 787-9 on the Mumbai-Frankfurt route as part of its post-privatisation transformation.
